title: fix(plugin-auth)!: a credential change ends access issued before it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D1WDVL9JpCQhTUF97fpymtZ)_

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/` teaches these auth doors; the behaviour is documented in `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` in this diff

## 维护者速读

- 用户改密码或重置密码后,改密前发出的邮箱变更链接、改密前打开的二次验证,以及改密那一刻正在进行的登录,一律不再算数;用户重新申请链接或用新密码重新登录即可,其他用户无感。
- 账户安全加固:替账户所有者保证"改了密码,改密前发放的访问就不再有效"。
- 若判断有误,受影响的正常用户只会被要求重新申请链接或重新登录,不丢数据;改动只在登录认证插件内,可整块撤回。
- 无

## What changes

One rule in `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: **a credential change ends access issued before it.** One predicate (`issuedBeforeCredentialChange`) over one clock (`readCredentialChangedAt`: the last write over the account's local credential row, read through the vendor's own `internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount`, the same row its password check reads, so the rule needs no data engine; the row's creation is the first password, not a change). Once an account's password changes, these, issued for that account before the change, no longer grant access:

- **An email-change link** (any link the email-change flow begun at `POST /api/v1/auth/change-email` mails, at either of its steps and to either address: the confirmation sent to the current address, and the link sent to the new one) minted before the change answers at `GET /api/v1/auth/verify-email` exactly what a never-issued link answers: `401 INVALID_TOKEN`, or the `error=INVALID_TOKEN` redirect to its callback. The global before-hook hands the vendor's door a value no signer issued, so the vendor answers through its own path. Issue time is whole seconds, so a link minted in the same second as the change is refused too.
- **A second-factor challenge** opened by a password sign-in before the change is ended at its verify door (its row and attempt counter deleted), which then answers what a never-opened challenge answers.
- **A door that ends the account's sessions when it sets the password** ends them again once the password is written: both reset doors, `POST /api/v1/auth/change-password` with `revokeOtherSessions: true` (the session it installs is kept), and the one-step invitation acceptance (ahead of the session it opens).
- **A password sign-in during which the account's password changes** is refused with what a wrong password answers at that door (email and phone), and its session is ended. The before-hook notes the credential the account holds before the vendor checks the password; the after-hook, first among the after-hooks, compares it with the credential held once the session is open.

Every door that overwrites the credential row counts, an administrator's `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-password` included. A check that cannot read its record refuses. Access issued after the change, and an account that never changed its local password, are untouched. No request, response or metadata shape changes.

This PR resumes a branch that was built earlier and never opened. On top of it, this round:

- merged `main` once (one conflict: `invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts`, where both sides appended a `describe` at the end of the file; both are kept, unchanged);
- checked the doors `main` changed since the branch point: none of the touched doors moved. The operator's password reset that `main` added writes the credential row's `updated_at` and ends sessions after its write, so the same clock covers it with no change here;
- declared the narrowing (`fix(plugin-auth)!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 disposition and a BREAKING note in the changeset);
- narrowed the claim in the changeset, the docs page and the rule module to the four things the rule covers, instead of "nothing issued before the change";
- put the after-hook's own docblock back on `globalAfterHook` (the new helpers had been inserted between them), and moved the session re-end above the ADR-0069 D1 comment block it had split from its `if`.

### Read first (by risk)

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`: `readCredentialChangedAt` (the clock over `internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount`, and the one-second first-credential window), `issuedBeforeChangeOf` (refuses when the adapter is missing or throws) and `refuseSignInAcrossCredentialChange` (ends the session it judged).
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts`: the sign-in refusal at the top of `globalAfterHook`. It runs ahead of the impersonation and second-factor after-hooks, and its throw sits after the lockout settlement, so the attempt is counted as a wrong password.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts`: the `/verify-email` token replacement returns early from the global before-hook (the request can only be refused from there).

### Two-minute check

After `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth^...' build`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts`. Expect `Tests 17 passed (17)`.

## Tests

- `credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts` (new, 17 cases), driven through the real routes (a real `AuthManager` over a real `ObjectQL` engine on better-sqlite3, behind `AuthPlugin.registerAuthRoutes` on Hono):
  - an email-change link minted before a completed reset, a `/change-password` and an administrator's `/admin/set-user-password` answers what a never-issued link answers, with and without a callback; the address does not move and no session is opened. Control: a link minted after the reset verifies and moves the address;
  - a second-factor challenge opened before a reset answers what a never-opened challenge answers. Control: one opened after the reset completes;
  - a session that a sign-in opens between a door's revocation and its password write is ended: the emailed reset, the texted reset, and `/change-password` with `revokeOtherSessions` (the session it installs stands);
  - a password sign-in during which the password changes answers what a wrong password answers (email and phone doors) and leaves no session. Control: a sign-in with no change stands;
  - a check that cannot read its record refuses (3 cases through the real routes): an email-change link whose clock throws gets the never-issued answer and the address stays; a second-factor challenge whose clock throws gets the never-opened answer; a sign-in whose first reading throws gets the wrong-password answer, hands out no session and leaves the session set unchanged. Each has a control that passes once the reading works;
  - the clock and the sign-in readings need no data engine: on the vendor's in-memory adapter (no `dataEngine`), a link for an account that never changed its password verifies, a link minted before `/change-password` gets the never-issued answer, and both password doors sign in;
  - every refused sign-in and race case asserts that no session token is handed out (header or cookie), with positive controls at each door;
  - the predicate and the clock, as pure units (string and `Date` stamps).
- `invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts`: one new case. A session opened before the one-step door writes the password is ended, and the session the door opens stands.

### Readings (local, final head `b5cbc6ad19f`)

All through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (VERDICT command-exit 0).

- Closure build (`turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/dogfood^...' --concurrency=2`): 70/70 tasks successful.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`: exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck` OK).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files 288 passed (288)`, `Tests 6050 passed | 10 skipped (6060)`.
- Full dogfood battery (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, no shard, no path): `Test Files 482 passed | 3 skipped (485)`, `Tests 4092 passed | 68 skipped (4160)`, no failures.
- Ablation, all legs inside one lock hold, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit once, mutation proven by blob hash, restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`); the test file imports from `src`:
  - A0 control, unmutated: `Tests 17 passed (17)`.
  - A1, an unreadable clock admits instead of refusing: `2 failed | 15 passed` (the link and challenge cases).
  - A2, a missing first reading lets the sign-in stand: `1 failed | 16 passed` (the first-reading case).
  - A3, the phone door takes no first reading: `2 failed | 15 passed` (the phone control and the in-memory phone leg).
  - A4, the clock and before-hook restored to `4cb593b8cc0`: `4 failed | 13 passed` (the in-memory case, the clock unit, both unreadable-clock cases).
  - A5, the refused sign-in no longer clears its session cookie: `3 failed | 14 passed` (each on "hands out no session token").
  - Earlier round on `4cb593b8cc0`: the predicate answering "not before" turned 6 of 13 red; the sign-in refusal never refusing turned 2 of 13 red.

## Acceptance notes

- **An account's first password is not a change.** The clock reads a credential row written over within one second of its creation as never written over: the row is created with its creation and update stamps taken separately.
- **Same-second issue.** An email-change link carries its issue time in whole seconds, so one minted in the same second as a change, after it, is refused too. Its owner requests a new one.
- **Fails closed.** A clock or record that cannot be read refuses what it was asked to admit: the link, the challenge or the sign-in.
- **No `Fixes` line.** This PR implements a seat order with no card.
